text: When designing REST APIs, it is important to follow some best practices. First, use clear and meaningful endpoints that represent resources, such as /users or /orders. Second, always return the correct HTTP status codes so clients understand what happened. For example, use 200 for success, 404 when a resource is not found, and 400 for bad requests. Third, provide good documentation so developers can learn how to use your API quickly. Finally, use versioning, like /v1/users, to keep old clients working when you make changes. Following these simple rules makes your API easier to use, maintain, and trust.
